# httpcache

```go
import "github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/httpcache"
```

Package httpcache caches whole HTTP responses of a handler in a gashe.Cache. A hit does not call the handler at all, and every strategy of gashe.Policy applies to responses: stale\-if\-error serves the last good page while the handler fails, Stampede.LockFor renders a cold page once for all processes, and Tags invalidate pages together.

Only GET and HEAD requests are cached, and only responses that are safe to share between users: see New for the rules.

<a name="New"></a>
## func [New](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/httpcache/httpcache.go#L123>)

```go
func New(c *gashe.Cache, o Options) func(http.Handler) http.Handler
```

New returns a middleware that caches the responses of a handler in c.

A request goes straight to the handler if it is not GET or HEAD, has a Range header, or has an Authorization or Cookie header Vary does not cover. A response is stored only if CacheIf allows its status and it has no Set\-Cookie, no Vary header beyond Options.Vary, no Cache\-Control no\-store, private or no\-cache, and a body within MaxBodyBytes; otherwise it is sent as is to the request that made it. A 5xx response counts as a loader error, so Stale.IfError answers it with the last stored response; a request Stampede.MaxLoads holds back, or one whose ctx deadline passes while it waits for a load, gets 503.

Request Cache\-Control and Pragma headers are ignored, so clients cannot make the handler run on every request. Responses get an ETag \(a hash of the body unless the handler set one\), Age on a response from the cache, and Cache\-Status \(RFC 9211\), with fwd=stale and fwd\-status on a stale page Stale.IfError answered; a matching If\-None\-Match gets 304. It panics on a negative MaxBodyBytes and on Policy.Negative, which cannot apply: CacheIf stores 404 responses.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/httpcache"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	page := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		fmt.Println("rendering")
		_, _ = fmt.Fprint(w, "<h1>Prices</h1>")
	})
	h := httpcache.New(
		c,
		httpcache.Options{Policy: gashe.Policy[httpcache.Response]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Minute}}},
	)(
		page,
	)

	for range 2 {
		w := httptest.NewRecorder()
		h.ServeHTTP(w, httptest.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, "/prices", http.NoBody))
		fmt.Println(w.Code, w.Header().Get("Cache-Status"))
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
rendering
200 gashe; fwd=uri-miss; stored
200 gashe; hit
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/httpcache/httpcache.go#L92-L104>)

Options configures New.

```go
type Options struct {
    // Policy says how responses are cached, as for gashe.GetOrLoad. CacheIf decides which statuses
    // are stored; nil stores 200 only. The rules of New apply on top of it.
    Policy gashe.Policy[Response]
    // Vary says which parts of a request a page depends on, and so what its key is made of;
    // Policy.Prefix is put in front of the key. The zero value means the host, the path and the
    // query, with requests carrying Authorization or Cookie headers past the cache. HEAD reads what
    // GET stored.
    Vary Vary
    // MaxBodyBytes is the largest body that is stored; a larger one is sent but not stored.
    // 0 means 1 MB.
    MaxBodyBytes int
}
```

<a name="Response"></a>
## type [Response](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/httpcache/httpcache.go#L78-L89>)

Response is a stored response. Policy.CacheIf receives it.

```go
type Response struct {
    // Status is the status code of the response.
    Status int
    // Header holds the headers that are stored with the page.
    Header http.Header
    // Body is the body of the response.
    Body []byte
    // ETag is the ETag header of the page, set by the handler or made from a hash of Body.
    ETag string
    // Stored is when the response was stored, for the Age header.
    Stored time.Time
}
```

<a name="Vary"></a>
## type [Vary](<https://github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/blob/main/httpcache/vary.go#L15-L36>)

Vary says which parts of a request a page depends on, as the Vary header of RFC 9110 does for headers, and so what the key of a request is made of. The host and the path are always part of the key; of the rest, only what Vary names is, so two requests that differ only in other headers, cookies or query parameters get the same page. Every part of a request the handler builds the page from must be in it, or one request's page is served to another.

```go
type Vary struct {
    // Headers are request headers whose values are part of the key: Accept-Language for pages in
    // the language of the request, X-Forwarded-Host behind a proxy that rewrites Host. A response
    // whose Vary names only these headers is stored; any other Vary keeps it out.
    // nil means none.
    Headers []string
    // Query lists the query parameters that are part of the key; the others, such as utm_source or
    // a random one, do not make new entries. nil means the whole query as sent; an empty list means
    // none.
    Query []string
    // Cookies lists the cookies the page depends on, such as a currency; their values are part of
    // the key, and requests with other cookies are cached too. nil means a request with a Cookie
    // header goes past the cache, unless User is set: its page may belong to who sent it.
    Cookies []string
    // User returns who the page is for, such as the user id of the session; pages are then stored
    // per user, and requests with Cookie or Authorization headers are cached. nil means pages are
    // shared, and requests with an Authorization header go past the cache.
    User func(r *http.Request) string
    // Custom returns anything else the page depends on; it is added at the end of the key.
    // nil means none.
    Custom func(r *http.Request) string
}
```

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>



```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/backend/memory"
	"github.com/eugeneliukindev/gashe/httpcache"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mem := memory.New(memory.Options{})
	defer mem.Close()
	c := gashe.New(mem, gashe.Options{})

	page := http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		n, _ := strconv.Atoi(r.URL.Query().Get("page"))
		_, _ = fmt.Fprint(w, "page ", n)
	})
	h := httpcache.New(c, httpcache.Options{
		Policy: gashe.Policy[httpcache.Response]{TTL: gashe.TTL{For: time.Minute}},
		Vary: httpcache.Vary{
			Query:   []string{"page"},            // utm_source and the like do not make new entries
			Headers: []string{"Accept-Language"}, // a page per language
		},
	})(page)

	for _, url := range []string{"/news?page=2", "/news?page=2&utm_source=mail", "/news?page=3"} {
		w := httptest.NewRecorder()
		h.ServeHTTP(w, httptest.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, http.NoBody))
		fmt.Println(w.Body, "|", w.Header().Get("Cache-Status"))
	}
}
```

#### Output

```
page 2 | gashe; fwd=uri-miss; stored
page 2 | gashe; hit
page 3 | gashe; fwd=uri-miss; stored
```

</p>
